quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When there are only a few vehicles on the roadway.
When drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. More following distance helps you avoid crashes.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. You should move around in your lane based on changing road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required for an effective eye or face shield?
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, fasten securely, and allow air to flow through. It should also allow room for eyeglasses underneath. It does not need to be airtight.

questions.question: What should a group do if one rider wants to go faster than the others?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep the group together.
Split up and let everyone ride at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster, let them go ahead. Plan to meet at a specific location later. This keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing makes you visible at all times. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing even in daylight.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing you?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and get closer to it. Once you are near, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick the dog.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tighter and speed up to get past the grooves.
Ride on the shoulder to avoid the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Just relax and ride straight across at the same speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows down your motorcycle, similar to using the brakes.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers happen at intersections. Be extra careful when approaching and riding through intersections.

questions.question: If your motorcycle chain or belt breaks, what happens?

options.text: The rear wheel gets more power suddenly.
The rear wheel loses power suddenly.
The front wheel loses power suddenly.
The front wheel gets more power suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel loses power suddenly.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to daytime?

options.text: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead at night.
Keep a shorter distance from the vehicle ahead at night.
Keep the same distance day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark. You cannot see shadows and light contrasts. You should increase your following distance at night compared to daytime.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear on a motorcycle?

options.text: Skip the jacket if the weather is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even when it is warm.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even when it is warm.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What defines a moped?

options.text: It must weigh less than 75 pounds.
The seat must be less than 15 inches off the ground.
It can produce no more than five brake horsepower.
It must not have a seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can produce no more than five brake horsepower.
questions.explanation: A moped is defined as a motorcycle or motor scooter with an engine that produces no more than five brake horsepower and a seat at least 26 inches from the ground.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips less than five miles long, just a few minutes after the rider starts.
